# Disclosures for the paper

This ledger collects every transparency item that the paper's methods, limitations or reproducibility statement must report. Items 1–5 are the principal disclosures. Section 6 lists smaller items already recorded in `PROTOCOL.md`. Each item gives the facts, the evidence file and the effect on results.

---

## 1. Lexicon B was generated by an LLM (the pre-registered fallback)

- No human co-author was available to write the test lexicon independently, so the protocol's fallback was used (`data/lexicons/LEXICON_B_LLM_FALLBACK.md`).
- **Model:** Gemini 1.5 Pro (`gemini-1.5-pro-002`), in a fresh, zero-context Python sandbox, on 2026-09-29.
- **Prompt:** the fixed prompt, sent once. The copy recorded in the provenance file is identical to the fixed prompt (checked programmatically).
- **Output:** 131 symptoms × 2 variants, 5–12 words each. No exact copies of any development-lexicon (A) variant. No punctuation fixes, and no edits of any kind.
- **Frozen at** SHA-256 `cd2a53e307926b4012264ae97229a25a6039638bbe5e10fc819c13208d91f78d` (`configs/lexicon_B_freeze.json`, commit `c92e434`), before the final evaluation.
- **Timing:** the model version, the session description and the "no punctuation fixes" statement were supplied by the author after the final evaluation had run. The file itself was frozen beforehand and is unchanged.
- **Evidence:** `data/lexicons/LEXICON_B_PROVENANCE.md`, `configs/lexicon_B_freeze.json`.

## 2. Two lexicon B phrases name a disease (39 queries); post-hoc sensitivity check

- **The deviation.** The fixed prompt says "do not mention any disease name". Two generated phrases break this rule:
  - "my **acne** is full of yellow stuff" (for *pus filled pimples*; Acne is one of the 41 diseases);
  - "my complexion looks completely **jaundiced** and off" (for *yellowish skin*; Jaundice is one of the 41 diseases).
- **Why they were kept.** The fallback procedure allows punctuation fixes only, so both phrases stayed as generated.
- **Reach.** They appear in **39 of the 530** lexicon B lay test queries: 23 lay full, 16 lay partial.
  - 38 come through "jaundiced". It is a correct cue for 5 Jaundice queries and a misleading one for 33 queries on other liver diseases.
  - 1 comes through "acne", on an Acne query.
- **Post-hoc check.** This analysis was not pre-registered. The 39 queries were removed and all results recomputed from the committed per-query outputs (`experiments/04_posthoc_sensitivity.py`).
  - Every system scores slightly higher without them.
  - The proposed system still wins every comparison, and H1–H4 all remain significant after Holm correction:

| | Group | Queries (all → reduced) | ΔMRR, all queries | ΔMRR, reduced [95% CI] | Holm p, reduced |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1: semantic vs exact KG | lay full | 181 → 158 | +0.302 | +0.315 [0.207, 0.417] | 0.00016 |
| H2: semantic vs exact KG | lay partial | 349 → 333 | +0.137 | +0.144 [0.077, 0.211] | 0.00102 |
| H3: semantic KG vs Hybrid | lay full | 181 → 158 | +0.290 | +0.306 [0.185, 0.420] | 0.00030 |
| H4: semantic KG vs Hybrid | lay partial | 349 → 333 | +0.141 | +0.149 [0.077, 0.219] | 0.00102 |

  The proposed system's MRR moves from 0.746 to 0.772 (lay full) and from 0.489 to 0.494 (lay partial).
- **Evidence:** `results/rebuild/test/sensitivity_no_disease_names.csv`, `sensitivity_no_disease_names_tests.csv`, `sensitivity_excluded_queries.csv`.

## 3. Lexicon B's line endings were restored before freezing

- **The mismatch.** When lexicon B was received, the working copy hashed to `1f8512cc…` rather than the recorded `cd2a53e3…`. The cause was formatting: Windows (CRLF) line endings and no final newline.
- **The fix.** The same text with LF endings and a final newline reproduces the recorded hash exactly. Those bytes were restored, and it was verified that no variant text changed.
- **Storage.** The repository stores CSV files byte-exact (`.gitattributes`: `-text`).
- **Effect:** none. The parsed lexicon is identical either way.
- **Evidence:** `configs/lexicon_B_freeze.json` (notes).

## 4. The latency script was written after the final evaluation

- **The deviation.** `PROTOCOL.md` §10.10 said the latency script "will be written before the final evaluation". It was implemented and run after the one-shot final evaluation (`experiments/05_latency.py`).
- **Effect on results:** none.
  - It uses query texts only, never labels, and does not feed any selection or test.
  - A guard confirms that the timed code produces exactly the evaluated scores (maximum absolute difference 0).
- **Result.** NVIDIA RTX 3050 6 GB Laptop GPU, one query at a time, 1,060 queries × 5 repeats after warm-up:
  - The proposed system takes **52 ms median (p95 168 ms)** per query, against **12 ms (p95 19 ms)** for the retrieval-only Hybrid.
  - Almost all of the extra time is semantic linking: SapBERT encodes each clause separately, taking 37 ms median, about 100 ms for full queries (about 8 clauses) and about 32 ms for partial ones.
  - KG scoring and fusion take under 0.1 ms.
- **Evidence:** `results/rebuild/test/latency_diagnostics.csv`, `latency_environment.json`.

## 5. Most final-test rows were evaluated in earlier project versions (148 of 181)

- **Counts.** Of the 181 v4 test rows:
  - **113** were queries in the v1–v3 test sets;
  - **131** once the v1 and v3 tuning validation sets are added;
  - **148** once two reconstructed v0 evaluation sets are added (the code does not record which of the two produced the v0 results, so both are counted).
- **What is untouched.** Only **33** test rows had never been queried. All 41 diseases are affected, and 18 diseases have no untouched test row. An untouched test set covering every disease was therefore impossible.
- **What was new at test time.** No lexicon B lay query and no 2- or 3-symptom partial query had been scored before. Earlier versions evaluated different systems on clinical wording and on dictionary paraphrases of these rows.
- **Indirect exposure.** The v4 design, including semantic linking and lexicon A, was shaped by knowing how v3 performed on many of these rows.
- **Why row identity protects little here.** Every row equals its disease's symptom set minus at most one symptom, so an untouched row is nearly identical to its touched siblings.
- **Evidence:** `audit/audit_test_overlap.py`, `audit/outputs/test_overlap_*.csv` (commit `ce96f94`).

## 5b. A second, hand-written test lexicon (lexicon C) was evaluated after the primary results

- **What.** After the one-shot primary evaluation with the Gemini lexicon B, a co-author supplied a hand-written lexicon (`data/lexicons/lexicon_B_human.csv`, called lexicon C in the paper). According to the project lead, the co-author had not seen lexicon A, lexicon B, the code or any results.
- **Checks.** 131 × 2 variants, 4–13 words, no exact copies of lexicon A or B, low word overlap with both (mean best Jaccard 0.20 and 0.18), no condition names.
- **Procedure.** Frozen by SHA-256 `ea4bf24d…` (`configs/lexicon_B_human_freeze.json`, commit `8a33114`). The unchanged system was evaluated on it once (`experiments/06_human_lexicon_eval.py`, output in `results/rebuild/test_human_lexicon/`).
- **Result.** It confirms the primary results: ΔMRR over Hybrid+KG-exact +0.328 [0.221, 0.428] on full and +0.148 on partial lay queries; over the hybrid +0.290 and +0.143. All four comparisons remain significant after Holm correction.
- **What the paper must say.** Lexicon B is the pre-specified primary test; lexicon C is a second test added after the primary results were known, with nothing tuned on it. It confirms the primary results; it does not replace them.

## 5c. Post-hoc robustness checks prompted by a mock peer review

These are not pre-registered: `experiments/07_reviewer_checks.py`, output in `results/rebuild/posthoc_reviewer_checks/`. The frozen system re-scored the lexicon B and C test queries and reproduced all 12,720 committed per-query ranks exactly before any check ran.

- **Untouched records.** On the 33 test records never queried in earlier project versions (23 conditions), ΔMRR over Hybrid+KG-exact on full lay queries was +0.415 (lexicon B) and +0.364 (lexicon C). All H1–H4 intervals are above zero.
- **Shared phrases.** Intervals were recomputed with a two-way bootstrap that resamples conditions and the 131 symptom phrasings. They are slightly wider, and all eight still exclude zero (H1, lexicon B: 0.185–0.410).
- **Tie bounds.** The graph-only systems depend on the tie rule. For KG-linked (β = 1), MRR spans 0.671–0.782 on full and 0.328–0.642 on partial lay queries. For KG-exact it spans 0.065–0.856 on full lay queries. The fused system has no ties. The paper therefore no longer claims that fusion beats the graph alone on partial queries.
- **Pool.** The hybrid's recall at n (0.497, 0.608, 0.757, 0.867, 1.000) caps any pool. Linear beats RRF on full queries at every n, with intervals above zero; on partial queries only at n = 5. RRF had no tuned weight.
- **Truncation.** With MedCPT reading the whole query (512 tokens) in both systems, the hybrid rises from 0.457 to 0.510 on full lay queries, and H3 falls from +0.290 to +0.237 [0.133, 0.339]. H4 is unchanged, because partial queries are never truncated.

---

## 6. Other items already recorded in `PROTOCOL.md`

- **Lexicon A.** The development lexicon was written by an AI assistant (Claude) after the v3 results had been seen. It was used for development only; on test rows it is a diagnostic (`data/lexicons/LEXICON_A_PROVENANCE.md`).
- **Protocol amendment v1.1** (§12).
  - **Change:** the proposed system's β grid was restricted to {0.05, …, 0.95}.
  - **When:** after the v1.0 development sweep had selected β = 1 (a pure KG model), and before lexicon B existed.
  - **Consequence:** the development sweep was rerun from scratch. The v1.0 outputs are preserved in `legacy/` and at git tag `dev-sweep-v1.0`.
- **Editorial change** (§12). Final outputs are written to `results/rebuild/test/` instead of `results/final/`. There is no methodological effect.
- **Development smoke runs.** During implementation, mechanics checks ran on subsets of development rows (§11.7). No test row was scored before the final evaluation.
- **MedCPT query length.** The standard 64 tokens was kept by the pre-set rule. 62% of lexicon B lay-full test queries exceed 64 tokens and are truncated for the dense encoder.
- **Near-lookup clinical conditions.** Because of the dataset's structure, the clinical-wording conditions are close to lookup (near-ceiling scores). The paper's claims rest on the lay conditions.
- **Dirty-tree flags.** The two development sweeps recorded `dirty: true` only because untracked audit files existed. Tracked code was verified unchanged against the recorded commits.
